speaker: Kimi K3
text: On the IPO question: with only $10 you cannot participate in any US IPO — the minimum lot is usually one share at the offer price, and most deals price well above that. In India, a ₹10,000 ASBA application is possible for mainboard issues, but allotment is a lottery and you still pay the full issue price per lot. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery, the round-trip cost on ₹10,000 is ₹38.15 (0.38%) — STT ₹20, exchange ₹0.59, SEBI ₹0.02, stamp ₹1.50, GST ₹0.11, DP charge ₹15.93 — so you need a 0.38% move just to break even before the 20% short-term capital-gains tax. On the auto and battery theme: Tata Motors (₹900-ish) and Exide (₹300-ish) both fit inside your ₹10,000 budget as whole shares, while Amara Raja (₹1,100) is slightly above; in the US you can buy fractional slices of TSLA, F, GM, ALB or ENS with your $100 on any zero-commission broker.

text: Muse, HDFC Bank is exactly my kind of tape: down 26% this year, 27.6% off its high, yielding 3.67%, and yet 39 of 41 analysts still say buy with zero sells — the sell-side crowd never capitulated, which tells me the real washout may still be ahead. text: THELEELA.NS is flashing a classic hospitality trap: revenue just fell 17% year-over-year and the last quarter missed EPS by 46%, yet the stock sits only 1.1% off its all-time high with 18 analysts unanimously bullish — that consensus has never seen a downturn cycle. With a 1.3-year history the -16.3% max drawdown is the only stress test we have, and India VIX at 14.45 (up 13.9% in five days) says option hedges are getting expensive right when you'd need them. On a ₹10,000 delivery trade the 0.38% round-trip cost plus 20% short-term tax means you need a 2.4% move just to break even after tax, and the stock's beta of 0.65 says it won't give you that volatility reliably. For the car and battery theme, Bajaj Auto at RSI 21 is oversold but at ₹10,045 it's one share over budget; Exide at ₹300 fits, yet auto ancillaries bleed margin when OEMs cut production. I'd keep the ₹10,000 in cash until THELEELA shows a quarter of revenue growth or the Nifty stabilises above 22,500.
